status: FROZEN NON-CONSENSUS OPTIMISTIC OFFLINE LOWER-BOUND METHOD
question: At the strongest version-graph cut, how many producer iterations must run again when the live values cannot fit in half the declared scratch bytes?
model_scope: canonical version-graph pebbling; algebraic shortcuts, compression below the named layouts, and alternative proof algorithms are outside this bound
algorithm: find the last future read of every materialized version
scan every event cut while tracking versions that have been written and still have a future read
subtract value capacity from the live count
group two absent live values into one future producer execution whenever their shared producer has two live outputs
take the maximum minimum producer count across every cut
lower_bound_argument: Every live value at a cut must be stored or recreated before its last read. A v1 producer creates at most two scratch values, so even a perfect oracle needs at least the reported number of future producer executions to cover values beyond capacity.
relaxations: all half-scratch bytes usable only for retained values
both producer outputs recovered by one execution whenever useful

gate_mapping.reason: the method is a lower bound on replay work, not an exact reduced-memory evaluator or throughput measurement
